Quiz – bored piles
What supports the wall of the bore when a CFA pile is made?
The soil plug remaining on the auger
A steel casing
Nothing – the concrete is placed immediately
While screwing down, the spoil is only partly pressed out; the soil plug remaining on the auger supports the wall continuously – no separate technology is needed.
In granular soil, how must the casing be advanced?
It must go ahead of the excavation
After excavation is enough, once the groundwater appears
Only below the groundwater table
It doesn’t matter, the casing supports it in the end anyway
If the excavation gets ahead of the casing, the free wall section below the casing collapses, the soil flows in, and the surroundings loosen.
What happens if, below the groundwater, the water inside the casing is lower than outside?
Groundwater breaks in at the base and loosens the soil
The casing floats up
The concrete sets faster
Nothing, the casing is watertight
The water level difference starts an upward flow at the base (heave): the water carries grains with it. That is why the water removed from the bore must be replaced.
When can an unsupported bore be used?
In cohesive soil, above the groundwater, to at most 8–10 m
In granular soil, if the groundwater is deep, to at most 20 m
In any soil, if we concrete quickly
Below the groundwater, if the bore is short
In cohesive soil, above the groundwater, for a bore that is not too long – and it must be concreted immediately after excavation.
Why doesn’t the concrete of a CFA pile need vibrating?
The flowing consistency and placing under pressure make it self-compacting
Because the CFA pile is unreinforced
Because the rotation of the auger compacts it
Because the soil plug compresses it
The concrete is pumped through the drill stem under excess pressure: the flowing concrete and the pressure compact it together.
What is necking in a CFA pile?
Narrowing when the auger is withdrawn faster than the concrete fills the space
Thickening of the pile head from over-concreting
Deflection of the drill stem in a hard layer
If the concrete flow does not keep pace with the withdrawal, the soil is pushed into the place of the concrete. That is why rigs continuously measure the concrete pressure and volume.
Which technology is NOT suitable for a pile 150 cm in diameter?
Cased bored pile
The diameter of a CFA pile is 40–120 cm; cased and slurry-supported piles are made up to 80–180 cm.
What is the most important rule in tremie concreting?
The end of the pipe stays immersed in the fresh concrete throughout
The end of the pipe must be lifted out of the slurry at the start of concreting
The concrete must be poured onto the slurry from the top of the pipe
The slurry must be pumped out of the bore before concreting
If the end of the pipe comes out, the new concrete falls through the slurry, mixes with it, and a slurry inclusion – a discontinuity – forms.
Why is loosened, settled soil left at the bottom of the bore dangerous?
It can greatly reduce the base resistance
It increases the shaft friction
It prevents the reinforcement from being placed
It doesn’t matter, the concrete displaces it
The pile base sits on the loosened layer – the base resistance can be much smaller than designed.
Which soil removal tool is primarily for granular soil?
Screw drilling head
The drilling bucket carries granular soil out in the bucket; the short auger is mainly for cohesive soil, and the screw drilling head does not remove but displaces.
